newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev ends flat on open, off midday highs.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev ends flat on open, off midday highs.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev eased to about 1,572-1,574 per dollar at the close on Thursday, little changed from the opening's 1,570-1,573, but off midday highs of 1,563-1,566 as dollar demand from importers rose, dealers said.
"A large fuel importer started bidding for moderate (dollar) volumes in the afternoon and banks raised their ask prices," one dealer said.
Foreign currency supply however was relatively large which prevented a further lev drop, dealers said.
The mark was bid at 922-924 levs and was offered at 925-927.

The lev has risen from Wednesday's close at 1,575-1,585 due to paring of forex positions by investors in lev-denominated instruments, hoping for a stable lev between 1,500-1,600 in the near term following appointment of a new reformist government on Wednesday.
The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) was spotted buying foreign currency at midday to contain the lev rise and boost its reserves, dealers said. BNB officials were not available for comment.
A cut in the BNB main interest rate, which becomes effective from Monday, has not pressured the lev, traders said.
The BNB informed banks earlier on Thursday it will cut its main interest rate to 43.08 percent annually from 51.48 percent, dealers said. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
